docs/agents/notes.md:73:- **`mix gen.controllers` dereferences `$ref` path parameters**, so declare shared path parameters once under `components.parameters` and `$ref` them (`- $ref: "#/components/parameters/SlugOrId"`) rather than repeating them inline. `path_parameters/2` resolves each entry through `resolve_parameter/2` — the parameter twin of `resolve_schema/2` — before reading `.in`/`.name`, which is what feeds both the action signature (`def show(conn, %{"slugOrId" => id})`) and the contract-test path substitution (`/api/inventory/items/1`). An **unresolvable** ref raises a `Mix.Error` naming the operation and the `$ref` (it used to be dropped, which left a silent `%{"id" => id}` signature and a literal `{slugOrId}` in the contract-test path). Treat a raise on a fresh stub as a typo'd component name.
docs/agents/notes.md:74:- **`mix gen.controllers` scaffolds per *slice*, not per tag.** A slice is named by the `operationId` prefix (`inventoryStructure.showDefinition` → `inventory_structure_controller.ex`); the tag stays the domain boundary and supplies `x-context`/`x-resource`. So one tag may own several controllers — the `Inventory` tag holds both `inventoryStructure` and `inventoryItems` — without the generator emitting a stub for a tag-named controller that intentionally does not exist. **Give every operation an `operationId` of the form `<slice>.<action>`, where `<slice>` underscores to the controller filename.** An operationId with no prefix falls back to the tag name as its slice.
docs/agents/notes.md:75:- **`x-context`/`x-resource` are still tag-scoped, so a *new* slice under a multi-resource tag scaffolds against the wrong struct.** Slices decide the filenames; the resource metadata still comes from the tag. For a tag owning several resources (`Inventory` declares `x-resource: PropertyDefinition`), a brand-new slice's stub will call `PropertyDefinition` context functions even if it serves Items. Every slice in the spec today already has a hand-written controller and is skipped, so this bites only when adding a slice: expect to rewrite the stub body, which the ADR 0003 clobber caveat already assumes. Fixing it properly needs per-slice resource metadata — do not bolt on a tag extension for it without an ADR.
docs/agents/notes.md:78:- **Guarding a test on a generated artifact must not `assert true`**: a parity test that fell back to `assert true` when `packages/api-client/src/client/` looked absent passed while asserting nothing, because its `Path.expand("../../../../packages/api-client", __DIR__)` resolved to `apps/packages/api-client`. ExUnit 1.20 only skips via `@tag skip:` (evaluated before `setup`); `{:ok, skip: "…"}` just puts a key on the context and the next `context.generated` raises `KeyError`. Use `DhcWeb.ClientParity.require!/1`. `mise run phx-test` generates the client (`pnpm --filter @dhc/api-client api:generate`) before `mix test`. Prove such a test fails by temporarily deleting an export before trusting it. `apps/phoenix/test/dhc_web/controllers/inventory_items_client_parity_test.exs` is the reference: it derives the operation set from the spec and catches a generated symbol missing from the hand-maintained `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` re-exports.
docs/agents/notes.md:79:- **Paginated Inventory reads project through `Dhc.Inventory.ItemProjection.project_all/1`**, not `project/1` in a loop: the single-item form issues its aggregates per row and turns a page into N+1. `project_all/1` plus `ItemValues.list_values_by_item/1` batch values, container/category summaries, open maintenance, and active loans across the page while producing an identical read model, so the derived label and availability cannot drift between the list and the detail read.

docs/agents/critical-patterns.md:156:- **Lock order is part of the contract, not just lock presence.** Commands that depend on a container lock that container chain `FOR SHARE` **before** the item `FOR UPDATE` (root first): a move locks the destination chain first; a restore locks the item's current chain first. That matches container archive, which locks the container (and its subtree) before any item row. Reversing either pair deadlocks. After the item lock come the dependent rows (the loan, the open maintenance period, the item's live loans). A command that locked the loan first — e.g. a member cancelling by loan id — deadlocks against one holding the item and wanting the loan. Since GH-508 (ADR 0023) this order is encoded **once**, in `Dhc.Inventory.AvailabilityCommands.with_locked_item/2`: a command reached by a loan id resolves the loan's `item_id` unlocked purely to learn *which* item to lock, takes the item lock, then re-reads the loan `FOR UPDATE` under it, so nothing is decided from the unlocked read. A restore peeks the item only to learn which chain to share-lock; if the locked row sits in a different container, the transaction rolls back and retries from a fresh peek rather than locking a new chain while holding the item. Add a new transition as a `run/4` clause under that primitive; do not open a new `Repo.transaction` with its own locking in `OperatorLoans`, `MemberLoans`, or `OperatorItemLifecycle` — those are facades.
docs/agents/critical-patterns.md:157:- **Constraint translation is centralized in `AvailabilityCommands.persist/1`.** It declares the partial unique indexes and the principal foreign keys on every changeset and maps them to domain reasons, and never uses a bang write. A race or an out-of-seam writer is `{:error, :already_allocated | :duplicate_request | :maintenance_open | :unknown_actor}`, never a `Postgrex.Error`.
docs/agents/critical-patterns.md:228:- Inventory quartermaster remote forms run their Phoenix call through `inventoryCommand` (`#lib/server/api/inventory-command.js`) with `inventoryManageOptions()`: list the form fields Phoenix may name and pass `propertyLabels` when the form submits `values`. Beginners' Workshop remotes do the same through `beginnersWorkshopCommand` (`#lib/server/beginners-workshops/command.js`) with a `formPath` map from `form-paths.ts`. Both sit on `commandResult` (`#lib/server/api/command-result.js`), the one success / `invalid` / `{ ok: false, error }` translation; a new command family supplies only its field attribution.

1: # ALE-276 — Mobile inventory and Loan workflow prototype
2: 
3: ## Verdict
4: 
5: The first release should use a **member browse-and-request journey** plus an
6: **operator action queue**. Physical actions (handover, return, movement, and
7: maintenance) begin by identifying one Item, then present only valid actions for
8: its current state. This makes the operational work possible on a phone without
9: turning the member browse experience into a quartermaster console.
10: 
11: The interactive, intentionally throwaway artifact is the authenticated Svelte
12: route:
13: 
14: ```
15: /dashboard/inventory/prototype/mobile-workflows?variant=member
16: /dashboard/inventory/prototype/mobile-workflows?variant=queue
17: ```
18: 
19: It uses local sample state only. In development, the floating control can also
20: be operated with the left/right arrow keys outside form controls. The switcher
21: is compiled out of production builds.
22: 
23: ## Journeys selected
24: 
25: ### Member: browse, decide, request, then collect
26: 
27: 1. Browse non-archived Items through free-text search and Category/property
28:    filters. Show the derived Item label, Category, identifying properties, and
29:    an availability badge with a non-personal reason when unavailable.
30: 2. Open one Item and submit `startsOn`, `dueOn`, and an optional note in the
31:    same mobile-sized request sheet. The request creates no entitlement.
32: 3. On approval, the notification and the Member’s Loan detail reveal the
33:    approved dates and the Item's home Container path. The Member brings that
34:    information to collection; an Inventory Operator records actual checkout.
35: 4. The Member’s Loan history is the place to cancel a requested or approved
36:    Loan before checkout and to see rejected/cancelled records. It is not mixed
37:    into general inventory browsing.
38: 
39: ### Inventory Operator: one shared, action-led queue
40: 
41: 1. Open a shared queue grouped as **requests**, **ready for handover**,
42:    **returns due today**, and **overdue**. Counts are operational triage, not
43:    ownership assignment; every Inventory Operator has equal authority.
44: 2. A request card has Member, Item, requested dates/note, and the single next
45:    decision: approve or reject. Approval collects the final dates/note and
46:    atomically reserves the Item and rejects competing requests.
47: 3. A ready-to-handover card shows the derived Item label/slug and Container path.
48:    After the operator checks the physical Item, the one primary action records
49:    checkout. A checked-out or overdue card similarly offers return. This keeps
50:    the retained Loan lifecycle visible without exposing invalid transitions.
51: 4. Item movement and Maintenance are Item-led rather than Loan-queue actions.
52:    After identifying the Item, an operator can move it (except when reserved or
53:    checked out), start Maintenance with a reason, or end Maintenance with an
54:    optional note. The backend remains the concurrency authority.
55: 
56: ## Labels and scanning — out of scope for v1
57: 
58: No physical Item labels, QR codes, barcodes, or camera scan in the first
59: release. Item identification is typed slug/search only; there is no
60: label-printing surface, no QR deep link, no scanner adapter, and no
61: barcode schema. Do not build them.
62: 
63: ## Search, queue, and reporting scope
64: 
65: First release search needs a server-side Item lookup over derived label,
66: immutable slug, Category, and property values, with Category/property,
67: availability, and archive filters. Members never receive Container as a browse
68: filter; operators may use Container as a location filter.
69: 
70: First release needs a dedicated operator Loan queue query filtered by lifecycle
71: bucket (`requested`, `approved`, `checked_out`, derived `overdue`) and due date,
72: plus small counts for requests, handovers, due/overdue returns, and open
73: Maintenance. These are operational views, not a general reporting system.
74: 
75: Defer utilization trends, member borrowing reports, export, stock audits, and
76: custom report builders until the club has real Loan volume. The selected queue
77: and retained Loan/Maintenance records preserve the facts needed to add them
78: without a new workflow model.
79: 
80: ## Implementation consequences
81: 
82: - Add a Member-facing inventory browse/detail/request capability distinct from
83:   Inventory Operator Category/Container management.
84: - Add Loan list/detail and queue contracts alongside the lifecycle decisions in
85:   ALE-273; return derived Item labels, slug, derived availability, and the Container
86:   path only where the viewer is entitled to see it.
87: - Add a slug lookup over the immutable slug alongside ordinary search. No
88:   label-printing surface, no QR deep link, no scanner adapter, and no barcode
89:   schema in v1.
90: - Ensure queue counters and search are projections/queries only; approvals,
91:   checkouts, returns, moves, and Maintenance remain atomic Phoenix commands.
92: 
93: ## Scenarios checked
94: 
95: - A Member sees an Item on loan but cannot infer the borrower and cannot submit
96:   a request.
97: - Two Members request the same available Item. The operator approves one; the
98:   other ordinary request is rejected, and the queue no longer offers it.
99: - An operator at the rack with an approved Loan sees checkout offered for that
100:   Item, not movement or Maintenance.
101: - An Item returns with a fault: record return first, then start Maintenance
102:   with its reason. There is no return-condition subdomain in v1.
103: - An operator identifies an Item by typed slug/search and performs the same
104:   action path; there is no scan fallback because there is no scan in v1.

1: # ALE-276 — Mobile inventory and Loan workflow prototype
2: 
3: ## Verdict
4: 
5: The first release should use a **member browse-and-request journey** plus an
6: **operator action queue**. Physical actions (handover, return, movement, and
7: maintenance) begin by identifying one Item, then present only valid actions for
8: its current state. This makes the operational work possible on a phone without
9: turning the member browse experience into a quartermaster console.
10: 
11: The interactive, intentionally throwaway artifact is the authenticated Svelte
12: route:
13: 
14: ```
15: /dashboard/inventory/prototype/mobile-workflows?variant=member
16: /dashboard/inventory/prototype/mobile-workflows?variant=queue
17: ```
18: 
19: It uses local sample state only. In development, the floating control can also
20: be operated with the left/right arrow keys outside form controls. The switcher
21: is compiled out of production builds.
22: 
23: ## Journeys selected
24: 
25: ### Member: browse, decide, request, then collect
26: 
27: 1. Browse non-archived Items through free-text search and Category/property
28:    filters. Show the derived Item label, Category, identifying properties, and
29:    an availability badge with a non-personal reason when unavailable.
30: 2. Open one Item and submit `startsOn`, `dueOn`, and an optional note in the
31:    same mobile-sized request sheet. The request creates no entitlement.
32: 3. On approval, the notification and the Member’s Loan detail reveal the
33:    approved dates and the Item's home Container path. The Member brings that
34:    information to collection; an Inventory Operator records actual checkout.
35: 4. The Member’s Loan history is the place to cancel a requested or approved
36:    Loan before checkout and to see rejected/cancelled records. It is not mixed
37:    into general inventory browsing.
38: 
39: ### Inventory Operator: one shared, action-led queue
40: 
41: 1. Open a shared queue grouped as **requests**, **ready for handover**,
42:    **returns due today**, and **overdue**. Counts are operational triage, not
43:    ownership assignment; every Inventory Operator has equal authority.
44: 2. A request card has Member, Item, requested dates/note, and the single next
45:    decision: approve or reject. Approval collects the final dates/note and
46:    atomically reserves the Item and rejects competing requests.
47: 3. A ready-to-handover card shows the derived Item label/slug and Container path.
48:    After the operator checks the physical Item, the one primary action records
49:    checkout. A checked-out or overdue card similarly offers return. This keeps
50:    the retained Loan lifecycle visible without exposing invalid transitions.
51: 4. Item movement and Maintenance are Item-led rather than Loan-queue actions.
52:    After identifying the Item, an operator can move it (except when reserved or
53:    checked out), start Maintenance with a reason, or end Maintenance with an
54:    optional note. The backend remains the concurrency authority.
55: 
56: ## Labels and scanning — out of scope for v1
57: 
58: No physical Item labels, QR codes, barcodes, or camera scan in the first
59: release. Item identification is typed slug/search only; there is no
60: label-printing surface, no QR deep link, no scanner adapter, and no
61: barcode schema. Do not build them.
62: 
63: ## Search, queue, and reporting scope
64: 
65: First release search needs a server-side Item lookup over derived label,
66: immutable slug, Category, and property values, with Category/property,
67: availability, and archive filters. Members never receive Container as a browse
68: filter; operators may use Container as a location filter.
69: 
70: First release needs a dedicated operator Loan queue query filtered by lifecycle
71: bucket (`requested`, `approved`, `checked_out`, derived `overdue`) and due date,
72: plus small counts for requests, handovers, due/overdue returns, and open
73: Maintenance. These are operational views, not a general reporting system.
74: 
75: Defer utilization trends, member borrowing reports, export, stock audits, and
76: custom report builders until the club has real Loan volume. The selected queue
77: and retained Loan/Maintenance records preserve the facts needed to add them
78: without a new workflow model.
79: 
80: ## Implementation consequences
81: 
82: - Add a Member-facing inventory browse/detail/request capability distinct from
83:   Inventory Operator Category/Container management.
84: - Add Loan list/detail and queue contracts alongside the lifecycle decisions in
85:   ALE-273; return derived Item labels, slug, derived availability, and the Container
86:   path only where the viewer is entitled to see it.
87: - Add a slug lookup over the immutable slug alongside ordinary search. No
88:   label-printing surface, no QR deep link, no scanner adapter, and no barcode
89:   schema in v1.
90: - Ensure queue counters and search are projections/queries only; approvals,
91:   checkouts, returns, moves, and Maintenance remain atomic Phoenix commands.
92: 
93: ## Scenarios checked
94: 
95: - A Member sees an Item on loan but cannot infer the borrower and cannot submit
96:   a request.
97: - Two Members request the same available Item. The operator approves one; the
98:   other ordinary request is rejected, and the queue no longer offers it.
99: - An operator at the rack with an approved Loan sees checkout offered for that
100:   Item, not movement or Maintenance.
101: - An Item returns with a fault: record return first, then start Maintenance
102:   with its reason. There is no return-condition subdomain in v1.
103: - An operator identifies an Item by typed slug/search and performs the same
104:   action path; there is no scan fallback because there is no scan in v1.

### First-time quartermaster workflow

1. **Confirm access.** The Inventory dashboard requires the `inventory.manage` capability; all holders have equal authority. [inventory layout](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/+layout.server.ts#L4-L10), [router](apps/phoenix/lib/dhc_web/router.ex#L245-L250)

2. **Set up the inventory structure first.**
   - In **Categories and properties**, create categories, then add the typed properties each item should carry: text, decimal, yes/no, or single-choice options. Mark required fields and optionally use a property in the generated item label. [categories page](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/categories/[[categoryId]]/+page.svelte#L608-L702)
   - In **Containers**, create a root storage location, then nest locations as needed. The UI prevents selecting an item itself or a descendant as a parent; moving locations by drag-and-drop is supported. [containers page](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/containers/+page.svelte#L72-L100), [#L489-L492]
   - Caveats: a category can only be deleted when no items use it; retiring properties/options can be refused until active values are cleared or migrated. Containers must have active children/items handled before archive or deletion; restoring requires the parent chain first. [categories](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/categories/[[categoryId]]/+page.svelte#L1221-L1229), [#L149-L165]; [containers](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/containers/+page.svelte#L113-L140)

3. **Add each physical item.** In **Items → New item**, choose a category and storage container, complete that category’s properties, and add optional handling notes. The label and permanent item code are generated by the system. [items page](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/items/[[itemId]]/+page.svelte#L229-L281), [#L305-L439]

4. **Maintain the register.**
   - Search/filter items; open **Manage** to update properties/notes, move storage, change category, or manage maintenance. [items page](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/items/[[itemId]]/+page.svelte#L510-L637), [#L1027-L1204]
   - Starting maintenance requires a reason; ending it can include a note, and maintenance history remains visible. [items page](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/items/[[itemId]]/+page.svelte#L1207-L1337)
   - Archive items that need a retained record; permanently delete only history-free items. [items page](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/items/[[itemId]]/+page.svelte#L915-L1005), [#L1344-L1369]
   - Do not move an item with a live loan. If an item returns faulty, record the return first, then start maintenance. [inventory workflow doc](docs/ale-276-mobile-inventory-and-loan-workflow-prototype.md#L51-L54), [#L99-L102]

### Loan workflow

1. **Use the shared Loan queue** for daily work: Requests, Ready for handover, Returns and overdue, and Open maintenance. It is a shared operational queue—not a personal assignment list. [loan queue](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/loans/+page.svelte#L293-L418); [queue design](docs/agents/where-to-look.md#L63)

2. **Review requests.** Open a request, set approved start/due dates, optionally add a member-facing decision note, then **Approve** or **Reject**. Approving reserves the item and rejects competing pending requests for it. [loan queue](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/loans/+page.svelte#L481-L528); [operator rules](apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/inventory/operator_loans.ex#L10-L16)

3. **Record the real handover.** From **Ready for handover**, check the physical item and select **Record checkout**. Checkout is only allowed during the approved date window and when the item is not in maintenance. For an early or late handover, update dates first rather than bypassing the rule. [loan queue](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/loans/+page.svelte#L324-L344), [#L530-L588]; [operator rules](apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/inventory/operator_loans.ex#L21-L29)

4. **Record returns.** Checked-out and overdue loans appear in **Returns and overdue**. Open the card and select **Record return**; update the due date first if necessary. [loan queue](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/loans/+page.svelte#L355-L366), [#L589-L617]

### Important loan caveats

- An operator cancels only an **approved** loan. A pending request is **rejected**; a checked-out item is closed by **returning** it. [operator rules](apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/inventory/operator_loans.ex#L17-L29)
- After checkout, the start date is immutable; the due date remains editable but cannot predate the handover day. [operator rules](apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/inventory/operator_loans.ex#L27-L29), [loan policy](apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/inventory/loan_policy.ex#L92-L101)
- Desktop drag-and-drop is only a shortcut: it opens the confirmation panel and does not itself change a loan. [loan queue](apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/inventory/loans/+page.svelte#L274-L279)
- There is no label-printing, QR/barcode, or scanner workflow in this release. [inventory workflow doc](docs/ale-276-mobile-inventory-and-loan-workflow-prototype.md#L56-L61)
